issue.title: Artifact-link index commits get one push attempt with no retry or aging, so a failed publication strands the commit indefinitely
issue.description:
Artifact-link index commits can land locally and never publish, with no retry and no
aging.

Proposed by epic phase bead sase-y3.4 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #2) while that phase
added the primary-sidecar dirt doctor guardrail; filed by the sase-y3 land agent
because phase workers may not create beads.

Epic sase-y3 moved machine artifact-link writes onto hidden host-owned sidecar clones
(`~/.sase/projects/<key>/repos/<role>`), which removes the eviction risk called out in
the current error text but does NOT close the publication gap: an unpublished commit in
a hidden clone is still invisible to every other machine and to the primary checkout's
pull-based auto-sync, which can only fast-forward to what the remote actually has.

task_type_fields.impact: A machine-lane artifact-link mutation that fails its single push attempt is silently absent from the remote: other machines never see it, and the primary checkout's pull-based sidecar auto-sync can never converge on it. Self-heals only if an unrelated later mutation happens to touch the same sidecar repo.
task_type_fields.repro:
Code path (read at master 63f385c9a plus the recovered sase-y3.3 tree):

1. `commit_artifact_link_indexes` -> `_unpublished_sidecar_error`
   (`src/sase/sdd/_artifact_link_commit.py:327-359`) runs only when a mutation just
   committed. It calls `push_bead_work_launch` exactly once, re-checks
   `head_is_published`, and on failure returns a human-readable ERROR string.
2. Nothing consumes that string as retryable work: there is no queue entry, no
   backoff, and no aging sweep. If the single push attempt fails (lock contention,
   network, non-fast-forward), the local commit stays unpublished indefinitely.
3. A retry only ever happens as a side effect of the NEXT mutation in the same repo.
   With no further link mutations for that role, the unpublished commit is never
   retried and no surface reports it. The hourly `artifact_link_backfill` chop does
   not sweep for unpublished heads; it only publishes what it just wrote.

Observed evidence (housekeeping lumberjack log, 2026-09-06 12:39:30):
`persist link indexes was committed locally but NOT published`.

Suggested remediation: give the machine lane an aging/retry sweep -- on each chop run,
before or after the per-project jobs, check each machine-lane sidecar root for an
unpublished head and re-attempt publication with backoff, surfacing a warning in the
chop report when the commit ages past a threshold.

payload.description: Same family of unowned post-commit failure: sase-xj strands a shared repo mid-rebase after an after-commit hook failure; this task strands an unpublished artifact-link commit. Both need an owner for the leftover state.
Both are follow-ups proposed by phase bead sase-y3.4 and filed by the sase-y3 land agent; the decision record should describe the machine write lane whose publication retry gap sase-ye tracks.
Adjacent retry gap: sase-xi resumes pending stitch hook-failure steps on finalizer retry; this task's artifact-link push is never retried at all. A shared retry/aging mechanism could serve both.
Same family of unowned failed-push commit: sase-ye strands artifact-link index commits after one push attempt; this bug strands a resumed main-repo commit without the marker the recovery lane needs
The event-publisher phase adds the durable retry/aging this bug tracks

payload.entry: Unchanged unpublished hidden sidecars are retried by the artifact-link backfill sweep with persisted backoff/aging, without requiring a later mutation. Landed as 46f7f549e (Python) and sase-core ff0a72e (v0.32.47 publication retry policy). Re-verified tests/sdd/test_artifact_link_publication_retry.py including test_retry_sweep_publishes_previously_unpushed_hidden_sidecar_commit and tests/test_axe_chop_artifact_link_backfill.py (14 passed).
